label: Acts 9:1
text: But Saul, still breathing threats and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest,

label: Acts 9:2
text: and asked for letters from him to the synagogues of Damascus, that if he found any who were of the Way, whether men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.

label: Acts 9:3
text: As he traveled, he got close to Damascus, and suddenly a light from the sky shone around him.

label: Acts 9:4
text:
He fell on the earth, and heard a voice saying to him,
“Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?”

label: Acts 9:5
text:
He said, “Who are you, Lord?”
The Lord said,
“I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

label: Acts 9:6
text:
But
rise up, and enter into the city, and you will be told what you must do.”

label: Acts 9:7
text: The men who traveled with him stood speechless, hearing the sound, but seeing no one.

label: Acts 9:8
text: Saul arose from the ground, and when his eyes were opened, he saw no one. They led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus.

label: Acts 9:9
text: He was without sight for three days, and neither ate nor drank.

label: Acts 9:10
text:
Now there was a certain disciple at Damascus named Ananias. The Lord said to him in a vision,
“Ananias!”
He said, “Behold, it’s me, Lord.”

label: Acts 9:11
Acts 9:12
text: and in a vision he has seen a man named Ananias coming in, and laying his hands on him, that he might receive his sight.”

label: Acts 9:13
text: But Ananias answered, “Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he did to your saints at Jerusalem.

label: Acts 9:14
text: Here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on your name.”

label: Acts 9:15
text:
But the Lord said to him,
“Go your way, for he is my chosen vessel to bear my name before the nations and kings, and the children of Israel.

label: Acts 9:16
text: For I will show him how many things he must suffer for my name’s sake.”

label: Acts 9:17
text: Ananias departed, and entered into the house. Laying his hands on him, he said, “Brother Saul, the Lord, who appeared to you on the road by which you came, has sent me, that you may receive your sight, and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”

label: Acts 9:18
text: Immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he received his sight. He arose and was baptized.

label: Acts 9:19
text: He took food and was strengthened. Saul stayed several days with the disciples who were at Damascus.

label: Acts 9:20
text: Immediately in the synagogues he proclaimed the Christ, that he is the Son of God.

label: Acts 9:21
text: All who heard him were amazed, and said, “Isn’t this he who in Jerusalem made havoc of those who called on this name? And he had come here intending to bring them bound before the chief priests!”

label: Acts 9:22
text: But Saul increased more in strength, and confounded the Jews who lived at Damascus, proving that this is the Christ.

label: Acts 9:23
text: When many days were fulfilled, the Jews conspired together to kill him,

label: Acts 9:24
text: but their plot became known to Saul. They watched the gates both day and night that they might kill him,

label: Acts 9:25
text: but his disciples took him by night, and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.

label: Acts 9:26
text: When Saul had come to Jerusalem, he tried to join himself to the disciples; but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.

label: Acts 9:27
text: But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles, and declared to them how he had seen the Lord on the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how at Damascus he had preached boldly in the name of Jesus.

label: Acts 9:28
text: He was with them entering into Jerusalem,

label: Acts 9:29
text: preaching boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus. He spoke and disputed against the Hellenists, but they were seeking to kill him.

label: Acts 9:30
text: When the brothers knew it, they brought him down to Caesarea, and sent him off to Tarsus.

label: Acts 9:31
text: So the assemblies throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace, and were built up. They were multiplied, walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit.

label: Acts 9:32
text: As Peter went throughout all those parts, he came down also to the saints who lived at Lydda.

label: Acts 9:33
text: There he found a certain man named Aeneas, who had been bedridden for eight years, because he was paralyzed.

label: Acts 9:34
text: Peter said to him, “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed!” Immediately he arose.

label: Acts 9:35
text: All who lived at Lydda and in Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.

label: Acts 9:36
text: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which when translated, means Dorcas. This woman was full of good works and acts of mercy which she did.

label: Acts 9:37
text: In those days, she became sick, and died. When they had washed her, they laid her in an upper room.

label: Acts 9:38
text: As Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, imploring him not to delay in coming to them.

label: Acts 9:39
text: Peter got up and went with them. When he had come, they brought him into the upper room. All the widows stood by him weeping, and showing the coats and garments which Dorcas had made while she was with them.

label: Acts 9:40
text: Peter sent them all out, and knelt down and prayed. Turning to the body, he said, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat up.

label: Acts 9:41
text: He gave her his hand, and raised her up. Calling the saints and widows, he presented her alive.

label: Acts 9:42
text: And it became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.

label: Acts 9:43
text: He stayed many days in Joppa with a tanner named Simon.

label: Saul asked the high priest for letters to the synagogues of Damascus
statement: Saul, still persecuting the disciples, went to the high priest and asked for letters to the synagogues of Damascus, to bring those of the Way, men or women, bound to Jerusalem.

label: Official letters to diaspora Jewish communities were a recognized instrument
statement: In the first century, letters of official authority to and for diaspora Jewish communities were a recognized instrument - the setting presupposed by letters from the high priest to the synagogues of Damascus.

label: Damascus had a substantial Jewish community with synagogues
statement: Damascus had a substantial Jewish community with synagogues in the first century.

label: The light and voice on the road to Damascus
statement: As Saul neared Damascus a light from the sky shone around him; he fell to the earth and heard the voice of Jesus asking why he persecuted him. (Miracle claim; searched, no external evidence found.)

label: The companions heard the sound but saw no one
statement: The men traveling with Saul stood speechless, hearing the sound but seeing no one.

label: Saul was blind three days
statement: Saul arose blind and was led by the hand into Damascus; he was without sight three days and neither ate nor drank. (Miracle claim; searched, no external evidence found.)

label: The Lord told Ananias in a vision to find Saul
statement: The Lord said to Ananias, a disciple at Damascus, in a vision, to go to the street called Straight and lay hands on Saul. (Miracle claim; searched, no external evidence found.)

label: Saul was staying at the house of Judah on the street called Straight
statement: Saul of Tarsus was staying at the house of Judah on the street which is called Straight, in Damascus, and was praying.

label: The man Saul was a man of Tarsus
statement: Saul, the persecutor then disciple, was a man of Tarsus (Acts 9:11, 30; also Acts 21:39; 22:3).

label: Something like scales fell from Saul's eyes; he was baptized
statement: Ananias laid hands on Saul; something like scales fell from his eyes, he received his sight, arose and was baptized. (Miracle claim; searched, no external evidence found.)

label: Saul stayed with the disciples at Damascus and preached in the synagogues
statement: Saul stayed several days with the disciples at Damascus and immediately proclaimed Jesus in the synagogues as the Son of God, confounding the Jews who lived at Damascus.

label: The Jews plotted to kill Saul; he was let down through the wall in a basket
statement: After many days the Jews at Damascus plotted to kill Saul and watched the gates day and night; his disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.

label: Damascus under the authority of the Nabataean king Aretas IV
statement: At the time of Saul's escape from Damascus (c. late 30s CE), the city was in some way under the authority of the Nabataean king Aretas IV, whose ethnarch guarded the city per 2 Corinthians 11:32.
note: Disputed: the fetched Wikipedia articles (Damascus; Aretas IV Philopatris) state that proposals of Nabataean control between 33/34 and 40 AD are contradicted by substantial evidence against Aretas controlling the city before 37 AD, that it could not have been a gift of Caligula, and that 'neither from archaeological evidence, secular-historical sources, nor New Testament texts can Nabatean sovereignty over Damascus in the first century AD be proven'; others read the ethnarch as the official of a Nabataean community in Damascus, not of the city as a whole. 2 Corinthians 11:32 is biblical and cannot attest its own claim.

label: Barnabas brought Saul to the apostles at Jerusalem
statement: When Saul came to Jerusalem the disciples feared him, but Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles; Saul preached boldly and disputed against the Hellenists until the brothers sent him off to Tarsus.

label: The brothers brought Saul to Caesarea and sent him to Tarsus
statement: The brothers brought Saul down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.

label: The assemblies throughout Judea, Galilee and Samaria had peace and were multiplied
statement: The assemblies throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace, were built up, and were multiplied.

label: Peter visited the saints living at Lydda
statement: Peter, going through all those parts, came down to the saints who lived at Lydda.

label: Peter healed Aeneas, bedridden eight years with paralysis
statement: Aeneas of Lydda, bedridden eight years because he was paralyzed, was told by Peter 'Jesus Christ heals you' and rose immediately. (Miracle claim; searched, no external evidence found.)

label: All who lived at Lydda and Sharon turned to the Lord
statement: All who lived at Lydda and in the Sharon saw the healed Aeneas and turned to the Lord.

label: Tabitha (Dorcas), a disciple at Joppa full of good works
statement: A disciple at Joppa named Tabitha (translated Dorcas) was full of good works and acts of mercy which she did.

label: Tabitha died, was washed and laid in an upper room
statement: Tabitha became sick and died; she was washed and laid in an upper room, and the disciples at Joppa sent two men to fetch Peter from Lydda.

label: The widows showed the coats and garments Dorcas had made
statement: The widows stood by Peter weeping and showing the coats (chitones) and garments (himatia) which Dorcas had made while she was with them.

label: Peter raised Tabitha
statement: Peter sent all out, knelt and prayed, said 'Tabitha, get up'; she opened her eyes, sat up, and Peter presented her alive to the saints and widows. (Miracle claim; searched, no external evidence found.)

label: It became known throughout Joppa and many believed
statement: The raising of Tabitha became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.

label: Peter stayed in Joppa with Simon the tanner
statement: Peter stayed many days in Joppa with a tanner named Simon.

label: Tanning, a noxious craft kept outside city limits
statement: Tanning was a noxious craft whose workshops (like the one of Simon by the sea at Joppa, per the later tradition) were kept outside a town's residential area.

title: Strabo, Geography 14.5.13 (Hamilton and Falconer translation)

label: Galatians 1:17 (WEB, bible-api)
title: Galatians 1:17 (World English Bible)
excerpt: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, but I went away into Arabia. Then I returned to Damascus.

label: 2 Corinthians 11:32-33 (WEB, bible-api)
title: 2 Corinthians 11:32-33 (World English Bible)
excerpt: In Damascus the governor under King Aretas guarded the Damascenes’ city, desiring to arrest me. Through a window I was let down in a basket by the wall, and escaped his hands.

label: Wikipedia: Street Called Straight
title: Street Called Straight
excerpt: Straight Street (Arabic: الشارع المستقيم) is the old decumanus maximus, the main east–west Roman road, of Damascus, Syria.

label: Wikipedia: Sarcophagus of Eshmunazar II (Sharon inscription)
title: Sarcophagus of Eshmunazar II
excerpt: The inscriptions also state that the "Lord of Kings" (the Achaemenid King of Kings) granted the Sidonian king "Dor and Joppa, the mighty lands of Dagon, which are in the plain of Sharon" in recognition of his deeds.

label: Wikipedia: Damascus (the Nabataean-control debate)
title: Damascus
excerpt: It is speculated that control of Damascus was gained by Aretas IV Philopatris of Nabatea between the death of Herod Philip in 33/34 AD and the death of Aretas in 40 AD, but there is substantial evidence that Aretas did not control the city before 37 AD

label: Wikipedia: Aretas IV Philopatris (the Damascus debate)
title: Aretas IV Philopatris
excerpt: Proposals that control of Damascus was gained by King Aretas between the death of Herod Philip in 33/34 AD and his death in 40 AD are contradicted by substantial evidence against Aretas controlling the city before 37 AD
